 --> GST decriminalisation decision marks shift towards trust-based governance, says CII
 Industry body says removal of arrest powers and higher prosecution threshold under GST will reduce uncertainty for businesses, particularly MSMEs, and offer a model for wider regulatory reforms 
 Ishaan Gera 
 November 02, 2026 / 06:11 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 GST decriminalisation decision a fundamental shift says CII CII hails GST Council reforms on arrest powers and threshold.
 Proposals include raising prosecution threshold to Rs 5 crore.
 October GST collections rose 23 percent to Rs 2.31 lakh crore.
 Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery
 Webinar by Vishal Malkan
 Find the weak links
 in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan
 Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE 
 The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has hailed the GST Council's decisions to remove arrest powers and raise the threshold for criminal prosecution as a landmark institutional reform that could strengthen trust between businesses and tax authorities.
 In a statement issued on November 2, CII said the decisions taken at the GST Council's October 8 meeting represented a fundamental shift towards proportionate enforcement and predictable tax administration while retaining safeguards against deliberate fraud and evasion.
 “The GST Council's decisions deserve special recognition as a landmark institutional reform,” said CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee.
 The GST Council recommended removing arrest powers through the omission of Section 69 of the CGST Act and increasing the monetary threshold for prosecution fivefold, from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
 It also proposed narrowing offences under Section 132 and rationalising imprisonment provisions. The changes would require legislative amendments before implementation.
 Related Stories
 GST collections rise 23% to Rs 2.3 lakh crore in October, fastest growth in over four years 
 GST reforms to be rolled out in phases from November 1, says CBIC member 
 Draft GST return forms to be put up on myGov.in portal on November 1 for public comments 
 CII said the reforms would particularly benefit micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
 “The importance of this reform is not simply that certain enforcement powers are being withdrawn. It is that the GST Council has recognised that effective tax administration need not depend on the threat of criminal sanctions,” Banerjee said.
 The industry body also welcomed circulars issued by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) on October 26, which sought to improve registration procedures and ensure greater clarity in notices and reasoned adjudication.
 CII said these measures, alongside faster refunds and input tax credit reforms, could improve working capital efficiency and reduce avoidable disputes.
 CII also urged businesses to reciprocate the government's trust-based approach by strengthening voluntary compliance, internal controls and responsible tax practices.
 GST collections in October rose to an over four year high of 23 percent to Rs 2.31 lakh crore compared with Rs 2.04 lakh crore in the previous month. October marks the fourth consecutive month this year when collections have hit over Rs 2 lakh crore.
 “The GST Council’s recent decisions to liberalise input tax credit provisions and allow refunds of ITC on input services and capital goods under inverted duty structures are exceptionally well-timed. These reforms can improve industrial competitiveness, support exports, stimulate fresh investments and further accelerate India’s growth trajectory while reinforcing fiscal stability,” said Vivek Jalan , Partner, Tax Connect Advisory Services LLP, a consulting firm while commenting on GST numbers.
